key_insight: AgentGym2 shows that current LLM agents, including top models, are far less capable in realistic end-to-end environments than standard benchmarks suggest.
engineering_relevance: For deploying agents in production, this benchmark highlights the need to test exploration, tool discovery, tool composition, and robustness to noisy or underspecified inputs.
method: Introduces AgentGym2 as a de-idealized evaluation framework grounded in real-world working demands.
Measures end-to-end execution beyond reasoning and planning, including proactive environment exploration and tool discovery.
Assesses robustness to uncertainty, noise, and unseen tasks requiring tool composition.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluated 15 proprietary and open-source models and found that even strong systems such as Gemini and GPT-5 struggle on AgentGym2.
watch_item: Because the benchmark targets real-world complexity, results may depend strongly on task coverage and the specific environment setup used in evaluation.
paper_title: AgentGym2: Benchmarking Large Language Model Agents in De-Idealized Real-World Environments
